claims.claim: American Tower sits between mobile/data demand and scarce physical hosting infrastructure: tower sites enable carrier radio deployment while CoreSite interconnection/data-center assets expose the company to data-intensive workloads. Q2 2026 evidence of robust tower leasing plus record CoreSite leasing supports this dual-infrastructure bridge, but does not establish that either demand stream is permanently scarce.

The principal structural substitute is not elimination of connectivity demand but architectural migration: carrier network sharing, small cells, alternative site owners, fiber/edge designs and more efficient radio architectures can reduce incremental macro-tower tenancy needs. CoreSite partly diversifies that risk but introduces separate data-center power/interconnection competition.

Successor bottlenecks are land/site rights, power, backhaul/interconnection, permitting and financing cost. American Tower remains useful when these constraints make replicated infrastructure costly; the thesis weakens if customers can satisfy capacity growth without additional leased physical nodes or if financing costs absorb lease escalators and organic growth.

risks.risk: Architectural substitution can decouple traffic growth from macro-tower tenancy growth.
Power/interconnection scarcity can shift value toward data-center ecosystems where AMT faces a different competitive set.

unknowns.unknown: How much future traffic growth converts into incremental AMT tenancy versus network efficiency or alternative infrastructure remains uncertain.
Durability of record CoreSite leasing beyond the reported quarter remains unproven.

claims.claim: Q2 execution does not falsify the operating thesis: revenue, property revenue, adjusted EBITDA, AFFO and operating cash flow increased and management raised outlook. The stronger challenge is quality and durability rather than current collapse.

Financing sensitivity is material for a capital-intensive REIT. The June 2026 10-Q reports $7.79 billion of operating lease liabilities and a 6.8% weighted-average incremental borrowing rate on operating leases, up from 6.6% at year-end 2025; this makes cost of capital and refinancing a present risk even while operations grow.

Reported net-income comparisons are vulnerable to currency effects, so AFFO and cash generation are more decision-useful execution checks. Carrier churn/concentration and lease renewal economics remain key falsification channels; no evidence reviewed here establishes an accounting defect or governance failure.

risks.risk: Capital intensity and lease/debt obligations create refinancing and rate sensitivity.
Carrier consolidation, churn or network rationalization can weaken tenancy growth despite rising traffic.
Using headline net income without normalizing currency effects can inflate confidence in execution quality.

unknowns.unknown: Current top-customer concentration and renewal economics were not independently quantified in this Beta pass.
Forward financing-cost trajectory and CoreSite leasing conversion require subsequent-quarter validation.
